summary: The bill amends the Anti-Terrorism Act of 1987 to classify the Muslim Brotherhood and its branches as terrorist organizations, bans their U.S. operations and bars members from visas or entry, requires the President to designate the group and qualifying branches as foreign terrorist organizations with corresponding sanctions, and directs the Secretary of State to submit annual reports to Congress identifying branches and recommending designations.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It focuses exclusively on terrorist designations, sanctions, and immigration restrictions.
No tax-related provisions appear in the bill text.
The bill does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

Section 2(d) adds new immigration restrictions by mandating visa ineligibility, inadmissibility, and revocation of visas for Muslim Brotherhood members. This directly expands enforcement and restricts entry pathways for a defined class of foreign persons, aligning with the restrict/enforce end of the spectrum.
No provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not authorize, modify, or affect military or defense spending.
No environmental or regulatory provisions are present.
The legislation does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education policy, funding, or school-related measures are included.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

While the bill imposes sanctions and designations related to terrorism (a criminal matter), these are foreign-policy and national-security tools rather than domestic criminal justice reforms, sentencing changes, or policing measures.
Sanctions may indirectly affect transactions, but the bill is not a trade policy measure and does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization frameworks.
No fiscal, deficit, or debt-related provisions exist.
The bill contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions modify, expand, or reduce foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or election-integrity measures are addressed.
The bill does not regulate technology, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, employment, or union-related provisions are present.

Although the bill targets an Islamist organization, it does so through terrorism designation and immigration enforcement rather than altering religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement frameworks.
